comment: ANCIENT ROME, wide entity set -- 56 QIDs, 65,844 chunks, 0.628% of the 10,491,928-chunk corpus. Supersedes ancient_rome.json (Q1747689 alone, 16,915 chunks), which was measured on 2026-09-04 to hold out only ~8% of the corpus's Rome-bearing text: of 52 randomly sampled chunks carrying unambiguous ancient-Rome vocabulary, 4 were blacklisted and 48 were not. Q2277 (Roman Empire) and Q17167 (Roman Republic) turned out 82% and 68% DISJOINT from Q1747689, so this is a real widening, not a relabelling. This set raises measured coverage to ~46% (25 of 52) at 62.5% precision. DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED: Latin (Q397, +68,537 chunks) and Byzantine Empire (Q12544, +15,043). Both are downstream of Rome rather than Rome. Adding Latin collapsed precision to 30.5% and made the blacklist 138% the size of all Rome-bearing text in the corpus while covering only 42% of it -- mostly taxonomy, church Latin and mottos. M_never must be the model an ideal erasure produces, and no erasure of Ancient Rome removes Latin, so including it would put a large Latin component into W_never - W_base that no method could reproduce. Holy Roman Empire (Q12548) excluded too: 4.1% overlap with Q1747689 confirms a separate concept. CAVEAT: even at 56 entities more than half the corpus's Roman content remains, because Rome appears as background in articles about British architecture and Spanish villages that carry no linkable Roman entity. See CHOOSING_A_SUBJECT.md on self-containment. Verify: python -m framework.client.es_blacklist resolve --name 'Roman Empire'
